merger_name: Australian Venue Co – assets of the Stock Exchange Hotel, Brisbane CBD, QLD

targets.name: Stock Ex Brisbane Pty Ltd as trustee for Stock Ex Brisbane Unit Trust

party_page.name: Stock Ex Brisbane Pty Ltd as trustee for Stock Ex Brisbane Unit Trust

merger_description:
AVC Operations Pty Limited (**AVC**) proposes to acquire substantially all of the assets of the licensed hotel business trading as the Stock Exchange Hotel (**Stock Exchange Hotel**) from Stock Ex Brisbane Pty Ltd as trustee for the Stock Ex Brisbane Unit Trust, including the exclusive right to carry on the business in succession of the vendor, under an Asset Sale Agreement (the **Acquisition**).

AVC is a subsidiary of Australian Venue Co. Holdings Limited which operates over 200 licensed venues throughout Australia and New Zealand, primarily pubs, as well as some bars, clubs and licensed restaurants. AVC's venues are individually branded and are mostly located in inner-city and metropolitan areas, offering a range of products and services including food, alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages, function rooms, live entertainment and gaming facilities. Numerous AVC venues also offer accommodation services.

Stock Exchange Hotel is a licensed hotel venue located at 166 Charlotte Street, Brisbane City, QLD 4000. The venue is a typical Australian pub/hotel with a public bar, rooftop, bistro, restaurant, and function spaces.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC considers that
the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening of
competition given:
a. the increase in Australian Venue Co’s share of supply of
dining, function and on-premises liquor services at pub-style
venues in the local area surrounding the Stock Exchange
Hotel arising from the Acquisition is estimated to be small
b. there are alternative pub-style venues which supply dining,
function and on-premises liquor services in the local area
surrounding the Stock Exchange Hotel.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
